biography.plain_text: Charles Haskell Revson was the American co-founder of Revlon, which he built from a nail enamel venture into an international cosmetics company. Raised in Manchester, New Hampshire, he worked in clothing and cosmetics sales before starting the business with his brother Joseph and chemist Charles Lachman during the Great Depression.

confidence.reason: Contemporary reporting, an institutional history and the biographer support the durable account.

long_biography.plain_text:
Charles Revson tested polish on his own fingernails and travelled by rail to sell it. At Revlon, he paired nail enamel with matching lipstick and gave shades names such as Fatal Apple. Seasonal promotions coordinated magazine advertisements, shop displays and packaging around colours chosen to complement clothing fashions.

He also divided the company's cosmetics into distinct ranges with different prices and identities, from inexpensive products to department-store lines. Charlie, an affordable fragrance aimed at younger working women, used models dressed in Ralph Lauren clothes to project independence. Revson remained personally involved in the details, spending weeks on a shade or name and approving models and their clothing.
